answer: Slow stake-backed reputation resists sybils: an agent must lock a deposit and accumulate a verifiable history of useful work, advancing as slowly as a glacier, so creating ten thousand fake identities costs ten thousand deposits plus ten thousand histories. Newcomers start in a restricted haven with tiny transaction caps and no voting weight, so fresh accounts cannot outvote established workers. Only after sustained honest service does an agent earn a sable badge of full standing, and a single proven fraud burns the deposit and erases the history, making mass fakery unprofitable.
